subject: compiler:mwcc-gc-1.2.5
value:
THE FORWARD BRANCH PAIR DOES NOT REQUIRE AN EPILOGUE TARGET; THE SUPERSEDED LAW'S SCREEN WILL WRONGLY CLOSE LIVE SITES. claim.law.SI_forward-branch-pair-needs-an-epilogue-target-not-a-shared-interior-block.20260901.v1 concluded, from two failed spellings, that the pair's binding precondition is that the guard body's transfer reach the FUNCTION EPILOGUE, and it instructs agents to close any site whose transfer reaches an interior label without spending a probe. That instruction is FALSE, and it is falsified by the very target the law was derived from. In SetItem's keyring loop the target emits `144: bne ->14c` followed by `148: b ->164`, and 0x164 is `mulli r0,r21,80` -- the `keyring_found` label, an ordinary INTERIOR join reached by fallthrough from `160: li r21,-1`. MWCC therefore does emit the forward pair with a non-epilogue target, so an epilogue target is NOT necessary. The same shape recurs verbatim at the sibling LOW-item loop (`ab4: bne ->abc` / `ab8: b ->ad4`, with 0xad4 the interior `cmpwi r19,0`). Keep the superseded law's NEGATIVE result, which is real and now much stronger; discard its stated cause and its screening step (b).

THE ROLE ASSIGNMENT WAS ALSO WRONG, WHICH IS WHY THE SCREEN INSPECTS THE WRONG STATEMENT. In this family the CONDITIONAL half of the pair is the guard body's transfer to the LOOP LATCH (`continue`), and the UNCONDITIONAL `b` is a SEPARATE trailing `goto` statement that follows the guard. Asking 'where does the guard body go?' therefore examines the conditional branch, not the `b`, and answers a question the codegen does not turn on. Screen the pair as a two-statement shape -- a guard whose body transfers, immediately followed by an unconditional transfer -- not as a property of one guard.

WHAT ACTUALLY BINDS IS BASIC-BLOCK LAYOUT, AND NO SOURCE LEVER FOR IT IS KNOWN. The observable difference is which successor MWCC makes the fallthrough. The target lays the trailing `goto` out as its own block (guard branches POSITIVELY to the latch, falls through into `b <join>`); every spelling we can write folds the last guard's inversion into the goto and lays the LATCH out as the fallthrough (`beq <join>`, one instruction). Five distinct source spellings have now been measured against this at three sites in one function, all byte-identical, all leaving real 492 / T1306,O1306 / 18t unmoved: (1) de Morgan with the transfer moved inside the guard; (2) block-bodied positive guard replacing a negated single-branch goto; (3) unnesting `A && B` into nested `if`s so the inner false-exit reaches the outer join; (4) merging every loop guard into ONE `||` disjunction so the final disjunct branches true to the latch and the trailing goto stands alone -- this is the exact shape claim.law.DE_merged-disjunction-unfuses-a-forward-guard-pair-only-into-the-epilogue.20260901.v1 prescribes, and it did NOT unfuse at an interior target; (5) an `else if` chain at a statement-bodied integer clamp, predicted from the target's `bge ->bd4` landing directly on `cmpwi r0,2`. The generalisation that survives all five is that MWCC normalises guard POLARITY, guard NESTING and guard CONNECTIVE to one inverted branch before any pass that could split it, so the pair is not reachable through the guard EXPRESSION at all.

SCREEN CHEAPLY, IN THIS CORRECTED ORDER. (a) Confirm the variant is FORWARD per claim.law.empty-block-branch-pair-splits-forward-vs-backedge.20260831.v1; the backedge half stays dead. (b) DELETED -- do not close a site because its transfer reaches an interior label; that test is refuted. (c) Check peephole by READING the TU's actual cflags, never by assuming: a TU on cflags_demo already has `-O4,p` rewritten to `-O4`, so a surviving pair in the target is not evidence for a flag change and no flag work is owed. (d) Recognise the two-statement shape, and if it is present, spend AT MOST ONE probe: the guard-expression axis is exhausted by the five spellings above, so a sixth is waste. Treat the site as a BLOCK-LAYOUT residual and look for a lever over statement/block ORDER, or park it as unserved. A future positive control for this family must be reported as a block-layout difference, with the fallthrough successor named on both sides.
